paragraphs.sourceText: Why it matters that teens are reading less
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么青少年阅读减少很重要

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Most of us spend much more time with digital media than we did a decade ago. But today's teens have grown up with smartphones. Compared with teens a couple of decades ago, the way they interact with traditional media like books and movies is undamentally diferent.
paragraphs.translationZh: A）我们大多数人花在数字媒体上的时间比十年前要多得多。但今天的青少年是伴随着智能手机长大的。与几十年前的青少年相比，他们与书籍和电影等传统媒体的互动方式有着根本的不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Analysis of surveys of over one million teens in the United States collected since 1976 reveals a major shift in how teens are spending their leisure time. Paper books are being ignored, in avor of screens. D屯ital devices are changing other behaviors, too. More and more, young people choose spending time on their electronic devices over engaging in other activities, regardless of the type. Indeed, by 2016, the average American high school senior said they spent six hours a day writing text messages, on social med团， and online during their ree time. And that covers just three activities, and if other digital media activities were included, that estimate would no doubt rise.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 自 1976 年以来对美国超过 100 万青少年进行的调查分析显示，青少年度过闲暇时间的方式发生了重大转变。纸质书籍正在被屏幕所忽视。 Dtunital 设备也正在改变其他行为。越来越多的年轻人选择花时间在电子设备上，而不是参与其他活动，无论何种类型。事实上，到 2016 年，美国高中生平均每天花六个小时在业余时间写短信、上社交媒体和上网。这仅涵盖三项活动，如果包括其他数字媒体活动，这一估计无疑会上升。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Teens did not always spend that much time with digital media. Online time has doubled since 2006, and social media use has moved rom a periodic activity to a daily one in the same period. By 2016, nearly nine out of ten young women in the 12th grade said they visited social media sites every day. Meanwhile, time spent playing video games rose rom under an hour a day to an hour and a half on average. One out of ten American 8th grade students in 2016 spent 40 hours a week or more playing video games. Let me emphasize that this is equal to the time most adults spend per week at work.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 青少年并不总是花那么多时间在数字媒体上。自 2006 年以来，上网时间增加了一倍，社交媒体的使用也从周期性活动转变为同一时期的日常活动。到 2016 年，12 年级的年轻女性中近十分之九表示她们每天都会访问社交媒体网站。与此同时，玩电子游戏的时间从每天不到一个小时增加到平均一个半小时。 2016 年，十分之一的美国八年级学生每周花 40 个小时或更多时间玩电子游戏。我要强调的是，这相当于大多数成年人每周工作的时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) If teens are spending so much time using electronic devices, does that mean they have to give up some other activities? Maybe not. Over the years, many scholars have 画sted that time online does not necessarily take away time spent engaging with traditional media or on other activities. Some people, they argue, are just more interested in certain kinds of media and entertainment. Thus, using more of one type of media does not necessarily mean less of the other.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 如果青少年花费如此多的时间使用电子设备，这是否意味着他们必须放弃一些其他活动？也许不是。多年来，许多学者认为上网时间并不一定会占用花在传统媒体或其他活动上的时间。他们认为，有些人只是对某些类型的媒体和娱乐更感兴趣。因此，更多地使用一种媒体并不一定意味着更少地使用另一种媒体。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) That may be true, but that still does not tell us much about what happens across a whole generation of people when time spent on digital media grows. Large surveys conducted over the course of many years tell us that American youth are not going to the cinema nearly as oten as they did in the past. While 70 percent of 8th and 10th grade students used to go to the movies once a month or more, now only about half do this. More and more, watching a movie is something teens choose to do on their electronic devices. Why is this a problem? One reason is that going to the cinema is generally a social activity. Now, watching movies is something that most teens do alone. This its a larger patten. In another analysis, researchers ound that today's teens go out with their 扣ends much less oten than previous generations did.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 这可能是真的，但这仍然不能告诉我们当花在数字媒体上的时间增加时，整整一代人会发生什么。多年来进行的大型调查告诉我们，美国年轻人不再像过去那样经常去看电影。过去，70% 的 8 年级和 10 年级学生每月去看一次或以上电影，但现在只有大约一半这样做。越来越多的青少年选择在电子设备上观看电影。为什么这是一个问题？原因之一是看电影通常是一种社交活动。现在，看电影是大多数青少年独自做的事情。这是一个更大的图案。在另一项分析中，研究人员发现，如今的青少年带扣子外出的频率比前几代人要少得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) But the trends related to movies are less disturbing compared with the change in how teens spend their time. Research has revealed an eno皿s decline in reading. In 1980, about 60 percent of senior high school students said they read a book, newspaper or magazine every day that was not assigned or school. By 2016, only 16 percent did. This is a huge drop and it is important to note that this was not merely a decline in reading paper books, newspapers or magazines. The survey allowed or reading materials on a digital device.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 但与青少年如何度过时间的变化相比，与电影相关的趋势并不那么令人不安。研究表明，人们的阅读能力正在下降。 1980年，大约60%的高中生表示，他们每天都会读一本没有布置或学校没有安排的书、报纸或杂志。到 2016 年，只有 16% 的人这样做了。这是一个巨大的下降，值得注意的是，这不仅仅是纸质书籍、报纸或杂志阅读量的下降。该调查允许在数字设备上阅读材料。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Indeed, the number of senior high school students who said they had not read any books or pleasure in the last year was one out of three by 2016. That is triple the number rom two decades ago. For today's youth, books, newspapers and magazines have less and less of a presence in their daily lives. Of course, teens are still reading But they are generally reading short texts. Most of them are not reading long articles or books that explore deep themes and require critical thinking and relection. Perhaps not accidentally, in 2016 reading scores were the lowest they have ever been since 1972.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 事实上，到 2016 年，表示去年没有读过任何书或没有享受过任何乐趣的高中生人数达到三分之一。这个数字是二十年前的三倍。对于今天的年轻人来说，书籍、报纸和杂志在他们的日常生活中的存在越来越少。当然，青少年仍在阅读，但他们通常阅读短文。他们中的大多数人不会阅读探讨深层主题并需要批判性思考和反思的长篇文章或书籍。也许并非偶然，2016 年的阅读成绩是 1972 年以来的最低水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) This might present problems or young people later on. When high school students go on to college, their past and current reading habits will inluence their academic perormance. Imagine going rom reading texts as short as one or two sentences to trying to read entire books written in complex language and containing sophisticated ideas. Reading and comprehending longer books and chapters takes practice, and American teens are no longer getting that practice.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 这可能会给以后的年轻人带来问题。当高中生进入大学时，他们过去和现在的阅读习惯将影响他们的学业表现。想象一下，从阅读短短一两句话的文本，到尝试阅读用复杂语言写成并包含复杂思想的整本书。阅读和理解较长的书籍和章节需要练习，而美国青少年不再进行这种练习。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) So how can this problem be solved? Should parents and teachers take away teens' smartphones and replace them with paper books? Probably not. Research has shown that smartphones are currently American teens' main orm of social communication. This means that, without a smartphone, teens are likely to eel isolated rom their peers However, that does not mean teens need to use electronic devices as oten as they do now. Data connecting excessive digital media time to mental health issues suggests a limit of two hours a day of ree time spent with screens, a restriction that will also allow time or other activities—like going to the movies with riends or reading longer, more complicated texts.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 那么这个问题该如何解决呢？家长和老师是否应该拿走青少年的智能手机并用纸质书代替？可能不会。研究表明，智能手机是目前美国青少年社交交流的主要方式。这意味着，如果没有智能手机，青少年可能会与同龄人隔绝。但这并不意味着青少年需要像现在一样经常使用电子设备。将过多的数字媒体时间与心理健康问题联系起来的数据表明，每天花在屏幕上的时间不得超过两个小时，这一限制也将允许时间或其他活动，例如与朋友一起去看电影或阅读更长、更复杂的文本。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The latter is especially important. I would argue that of all the changes brought about by the widespread use of digital devices, the huge decline in reading is likely to have the biggest negative impact on today's teens because reading books and longer articles is one of the best ways to lean critical thinking. It helps people to understand complex issues and to separate act rom iction. Thus, deep reading is crucial or being a good citizen, a successul college student nd a productive employee. If serious reading d比s, a lot will go with it.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 后者尤其重要。我认为，在数字设备的广泛使用带来的所有变化中，阅读量的大幅下降可能对当今的青少年产生最大的负面影响，因为阅读书籍和较长的文章是培养批判性思维的最佳方法之一。它帮助人们理解复杂的问题并将行为与行为分开。因此，深度阅读对于成为一名好公民、一名成功的大学生和一名高效的员工至关重要。如果认真阅读，很多东西都会随之而来。
